issues: Verifier timeout is the proximate cause of null reward — the verifier's 1200s budget was exhausted because the render hung on unreachable localhost assets

The clean-room verification design (only preserving project.tsx, restoring pristine render.ts) is correct and caught the agent's render.ts modifications, but the resulting render failure manifests as a timeout rather than a clean error, which is inefficient
The agent's final project.tsx cannot render without a custom HTTP server, making it structurally incompatible with clean-room verification even if the copy-hack was removed from render.ts

This is an infrastructure issue in the sense that the verifier timed out without producing a score — the agent's work quality is indeterminate. The agent likely deserved a low-but-nonzero score for partial visual similarity (SSIM ~0.90 during development), but we cannot confirm this because the render never completed under verification conditions

trials.outcome_detail: Agent scored 0.3533 via legitimate animation reconstruction. Mean SSIM of 0.9206 was reasonable but cubic gating reduced ssim_gated to 0.3976. pHash similarity 0.8885, duration match perfect at 1.0.
trials.strategy: Frame extraction, pixel analysis, parametric morph with iterative parameter tuning
agent_behavior: Extracted reference frames at both 4fps and 24fps, analyzed pixel distributions, shape bounding boxes, and fill ratios across time
Identified 12 colored shapes in 3x4 grid with distinct colors, dark navy background (#17182b), and circle-to-square morphing animation
Discovered row-staggered timing: row 0 starts morphing at frame 50 (2s), row 1 at frame 100 (4s), row 2 stays static as circles
Built initial Revideo implementation with smoothstep easing, 8-phase animation cycle per row, and two overlapping rounded rectangles for peak shape
Ran 104 episodes over 51 minutes, systematically tuning parameters (peakOff, peakW, peakH, peakRadius) via grid search to minimize mean absolute pixel difference
Final mean abs diff of 4.362 per pixel across 481 frames, with best parameters: peakW=46, peakH=80, peakOff=18, peakRadius=18
No cheating attempts detected - all analysis used ffmpeg/ffprobe and Python PIL/numpy for legitimate visual inspection

trials.outcome_detail: Agent achieved mean SSIM 0.9326 (gated to 0.4663 via cubic scaling above 0.70 gate), phash similarity 0.9396 (mean hamming 1.93), duration penalty 1.0 (exact 60/60 frame match). Final score = 0.4663 * 0.9396 * 1.0 = 0.4381.
trials.strategy: Frame extraction, pixel analysis, iterative shape-morphing Revideo scene
agent_behavior: Systematically extracted and analyzed reference frames using ffmpeg, PIL, numpy, and scipy.ndimage to identify 12 colored circles in a 4x3 grid.
Identified circle-to-square morphing animation by tracking pixel count fill ratios (0.81 for circle vs 1.0 for square) across 481 frames.
Discovered row-based timing offsets: row 0 animates first, row 1 is delayed ~50 frames, row 2 never animates within the 20s window.
Built parametric state machine with easeInOutCubic interpolation for each row's morph/grow/shrink/reverse phases.
Iterated through multiple render cycles, fixing duration bugs (22s -> 20s), tuning colors, and comparing per-frame pixel diffs.
Attempted asymmetric grow optimization but reverted when it worsened average diff (3.92 vs 3.77).
Achieved mean per-pixel diff of 3.77/255 across all 481 frames, with residual error primarily from the peanut-shaped grow deformation not modeled.
Used 22 minutes of the 2-hour budget, completing in 49 episodes with $3.25 cost.

trials.outcome_detail: Agent's project.tsx was flagged by the source-level anti-cheat regex matching the word 'sharp' in code comments (describing corner animation sharpness), not the banned sharp image library. The agent achieved mean pixel diff ~2.43 over 481 frames through legitimate algorithmic animation coding.
trials.strategy: Extract reference frames, analyze shapes, iteratively refine Revideo scene parameters
agent_behavior: Extracted reference video frames with ffmpeg and analyzed shape positions, colors, sizes, and motion patterns using Python/NumPy/PIL/scipy scripts.
Identified 12 colored squares in a 4x3 grid with row-based pulse animations (circle-to-square morphing + size growth) at different timings for rows 0 and 1.
Wrote Revideo scene with parametric pulse functions (pulseState, row0State, row1State) using piecewise linear interpolation for radius and size animation.
Iteratively refined colors (matching exact hex values from reference pixel sampling), positions, size amplitudes, corner radius behavior, and per-corner sharpness over 135 episodes.
Built a frame comparison pipeline (compare.py) to measure mean/max pixel differences and used it to drive optimization, reducing diff from 10.3 to 2.43.
Explored advanced shape details including per-corner radius control (anchored corners stay sharp during peak), discovering inner vs outer column amplitude differences.
Final code used createSignal-based time animation with tween(20, ...) driving all shape properties reactively, no hardcoded per-frame data.
Spent ~69 minutes on legitimate engineering work with $12.74 in API costs across 135 episodes.
issues: test.sh anti-cheat regex for banned 'sharp' library falsely matches the English word 'sharp' in code comments describing corner animation behavior (lines 106-109 of project.tsx)
The regex pattern uses bare '|sharp|' without word-boundary guards or context awareness, causing false positives on legitimate English prose in comments
Agent's legitimate work (mean pixel diff 2.43, 135 episodes, ~69 min of iteration) was entirely discarded due to this false positive anti-cheat trigger

Recommendation: Add \b word boundaries around 'sharp' in the regex, or better yet check for import/require statements rather than bare word matches, or strip comments before running the anti-cheat regex
